subject: measurementInvarianceCat and multiple-group analysis with categorical data

messages.author: fceb9ab059ad5d39
messages.subject: measurementInvarianceCat and multiple-group analysis with categorical data
parts:
Dear list,

I am running multiple-group CFA with categorical data (no missing data). The model is very simple, and everything seems fine with the conventional lavaan code. Then I turn to measurementInvarianceCat function. Surprisingly, the results look different. In particular, the chi-square and degree of freedom are calculated differently. Can anyone please let me know what causes this?

model <- "M =~ M1 + M2 + M3 + M4 + M5 + M6"
config <- cfa(model, data=M3, ordered=c("M1", "M2", "M3", "M4", "M5", "M6"),std.lv=TRUE,group="gender", parameterization="theta")
weak <- cfa(model, data=M3, ordered=c("M1", "M2", "M3", "M4", "M5", "M6"),std.lv=TRUE, group="gender", group.equal=c("loadings"), parameterization="theta")
strong<-cfa(model, data=M3, ordered=c("M1", "M2", "M3", "M4", "M5", "M6"),std.lv=TRUE, group="gender", group.equal=c("loadings", "thresholds"), parameterization="theta")
strict <- cfa(model, data=M3, ordered=c("M1", "M2", "M3", "M4", "M5", "M6"),std.lv=TRUE, group="gender", group.equal=c("loadings", "thresholds", "residuals"), parameterization="theta")

Chi-sq:
config: 27.977 (df: 18)
weak: 35.917 (df: 24)
strong: 32.818 (df: 29)
strict: 40.399 (df: 35)

(Note: the chi-square for the strong model is smalled than that for the weak model. Is it normal?)

measurementInvarianceCat(model, data = M3, group = "gender", parameterization="theta", ordered = c("M1", "M2", "M3", "M4", "M5", "M6"),std.lv=TRUE,strict = TRUE,estimator="DWLS",method = "satorra.bentler.2001")

Results:
Chi Square Difference Test

               Df AIC BIC   Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)    
fit.configural 18          27.977                                  
fit.loadings   23          29.079      1.102       5     0.9539    
fit.thresholds 28          32.546      3.467       5     0.6284    
fit.residuals  34          39.790      7.244       6     0.2989    
fit.means      35         128.242     88.452       1     <2e-16 ***

messages.subject: Re: measurementInvarianceCat and multiple-group analysis with categorical data
parts:
The authors of semTools::measurementInvarianceCat() has a description of the procedure he follows (Millsap & Yun-Tein, 2004) on his web site, so you can check whether you are imposing the same constraints he does.

http://www.myweb.ttu.edu/spornpra/catInvariance.html

Below the procedural descriptions for 5- and 2-category items, respectively, there are links to lavaan scripts (and Mplus).  It would be a good place to start looking for an answer.

Terry

messages.author: fceb9ab059ad5d39
messages.subject: Re: measurementInvarianceCat and multiple-group analysis with categorical data
parts: Just to update on this, I finally found out where the difference in degree of freedom came from. It seems that measurementInvarianceCat does not recognise std.lv=TRUE. When this argument is removed, the results are comparable between the two methods.
